title: Distance Structure of Insertion Kernels and Local Port Response in Non-Reciprocal Su--Schrieffer--Heeger Chains
abstract: Non-reciprocal lattices offer a flexible setting for directional wave transport, raising the question of how enhanced internal scattering translates into transmission between fixed external ports. We address this question for non-reciprocal Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) chains with staggered gain and loss by relating the reference-dependent insertion kernel $K_p=VG_pV$ to the coherent transmission intensity $T$. On a fixed finite graph, a strong-insertion expansion gives a contribution proportional to $γ^{1-d}$, whose coefficient is the signed sum of shortest directed paths of length $d$. When this sum is nonzero, it sets the leading behavior independently of fixed diagonal losses; when it cancels, those losses can enter the first surviving higher-order term. For a fixed cross-sublattice endpoint channel, transmission has a strictly negative slope at every nonzero differentiable stationary point of the kernel magnitude. In the weak-insertion regime, the reference-system coefficient $χ=-\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Tr}[(G_{0p}Z)^2]$ predicts the initial transmission change for symmetric SSH ports, and $χ>0$ together with a strictly stable baseline guarantees local stable enhancement. Finite-chain calculations and driven dynamics connect these results to observable response and distinguish asymptotic convergence from transient settling. A strictly dissipative short-chain example exhibits local enhancement without net power gain. Together, these results separate graph-path structure, coherent port response, and dynamical establishment, providing channel-specific criteria for interpreting internal scattering.
summary: This work analyzes non-reciprocal SSH chains to understand how internal scattering affects external signal transmission. It develops theoretical tools to separate the contributions from graph path structure, coherent port response, and dynamic settling. The findings offer clear criteria for predicting local transmission enhancement based on system parameters.
main_problem: The paper investigates how enhanced internal scattering in non-reciprocal lattices translates into measurable transmission between fixed external ports.
main_result: The leading behavior of the end-to-end kernel is determined by the signed sum of shortest directed paths, and local enhancement can be predicted by the coefficient $\chi$ in the weak-insertion regime.
method: The analysis uses resolvent techniques, strong-insertion expansions, and similarity transformations to relate the insertion kernel $K_p$ to the coherent transmission intensity $T$.
model_or_system: The model is a non-reciprocal Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain incorporating staggered gain and loss, analyzed using non-Hermitian Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Coherent transmission intensity ($T$), insertion kernel ($K_p$), and the local predictive coefficient ($\chi$).
important_parameters: The gain/loss parameter ($\gamma$), the chain length ($N$), and the degree of non-reciprocity.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fixed frequency baselines and assumes the separation of graph-path structure, coherent port response, and dynamical establishment.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the distance scaling of the end-to-end insertion kernel $|(K_p)_{B N-1, A0}|$ versus $\gamma/J$ for various chain lengths, confirming power-law decay.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by relating the insertion kernel to path sums in the strong-insertion limit, analyzes the weak-insertion limit using the coefficient $\chi$, and finally separates the total response into three distinct physical contributions.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous, channel-specific criteria for interpreting internal scattering effects in open, non-Hermitian quantum systems, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems.
